hypotheses.justification: The equality still holds when n = 0, and it follows from the stated (n > 0) case by multiplying r by the chart element. Write a := i.2 and m := i.1 > 0. Then r * a ∈ 𝒜 (n + m) by SetLike.mul_mem_graded, and n + m > 0, so the theorem as stated applies to r * a. Proj.basicOpen_mul (Mathlib, ProjectiveSpectrum/Basic.lean) gives basicOpen 𝒜 (r*a) = basicOpen 𝒜 r ⊓ basicOpen 𝒜 a. Preimages commute with ⊓. The chart map degreeScaledChartMap is defined as … ≫ awayι 𝒜 a, and opensRange_awayι says the range of awayι 𝒜 a is basicOpen 𝒜 a. So the preimage of basicOpen 𝒜 a under the chart map is ⊤, and the left side for r*a equals the left side for r. On the right side, f (r*a) = f r * f a, so basicOpen ℬ (f(r*a)) = basicOpen ℬ (f r) ⊓ basicOpen ℬ (f a). The preimage of basicOpen ℬ (f a) under (basicOpen ℬ (f a)).ι is ⊤, so that side also reduces to the side for r. Mathematically: for a homogeneous prime p in D(a), s ∈ p ↔ s*a ∈ p, so the degree-0 case is the same as the positive-degree case. The only step in the proof that uses hn is the call to Mathlib's awayι_preimage_basicOpen, and the reduction above avoids it.

The statement also holds for any r, not only homogeneous ones, provided hn is kept (n is then constrained only by hn). First, the homogeneous case holds in every degree k, including k = 0, by the argument given for hn. For arbitrary r, Proj.basicOpen_eq_union_of_projection (Mathlib, ProjectiveSpectrum/Basic.lean, line 77) gives basicOpen 𝒜 r = ⨆ k, basicOpen 𝒜 (proj k r). Preimages commute with ⨆, so the left side is ⨆ k of the preimage of basicOpen ℬ (f (proj k r)) under the ι map. Next, f r = Σ_k f(proj k r) with f(proj k r) ∈ ℬ (d*k) by hdeg. Because hd gives d > 0, the degrees d*k are pairwise distinct, so f(proj k r) is exactly the (d*k)-component of f r and the other components are 0. A homogeneous prime q contains f r iff it contains every component of f r, i.e. iff it contains every f(proj k r). Hence basicOpen ℬ (f r) = ⨆ k, basicOpen ℬ (f (proj k r)), and the two sides agree. This proof is longer than the one for hn but needs only standard decomposition facts.
